subject: Culture
title: Corporate Gift Culture
description: A fast breakdown of Corporate Gift Culture for builders.

hook.text: Japan's 'Ochugen' and 'Oseibo' gift seasons require employees to send presents to bosses twice a year—no exceptions.

buildup.text: In Japan, business gifting is codified. Gift value must match hierarchy: seniors get premium, juniors get standard.

discovery.text: American tech companies give branded merchandise. Chinese firms give red envelopes. German firms give quality tools.

twist.text: Gift-giving bans in Western compliance culture puzzle Asian partners. Refusing a gift is refusing the relationship.

climax.text: Savvy firms adapt: they accept gifts gracefully, report them to compliance, and reciprocate within allowed limits.

punchline.text: Global business runs on knowing when a gift is a gesture and when it's a trap.

quiz.question: What are the two Japanese corporate gift-giving seasons?
